rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day alternate, each following the other, as in the verse about their succession.
rows.anchor: واعتقابهما لأن كل واحد منهما يعقب الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships benefit people through their cargo, or through other benefits they provide.
rows.anchor: بالذي ينفعهم مما يحمل فيها أو ينفع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing coordinates spreading creatures with what God sent down, within the relative clause describing the water.
rows.anchor: عطف على انزل داخل تحت حكم الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, spreading creatures coordinates with reviving the earth: rain revives it and fertility sustains its creatures.
rows.anchor: فأحيا بالمطر الأرض وبث فيها من كل دابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds vary in direction and in being hot, cold, violent, gentle, barren, or fertilizing.
rows.anchor: في مهابها قبولا ودبورا وجنوبا وشمالا وفي احوالها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation says the winds alternate between mercy and punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل تارة بالرحمة وتارة بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjects clouds to winds, turning them through the air by His will and raining wherever He wills.
rows.anchor: سخر للرياح تقلبه في الجو بمشيئة الله يمطر حيث شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational observers recognize these signs as evidence of God's immense power and striking wisdom.
rows.anchor: لأنها دلائل على عظيم القدرة وباهر الحكمة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns readers who recite this verse without reflecting or learning from it; no grading is supplied.
rows.anchor: ويل لمن قرأ هذه الآية فمج بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include al-fulk with two dammas and the singular الريح.
rows.anchor: بضمتين ( وتصريف الريح ) على الافراد

none: source text is broken; only an opening quotation mark is present

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says people could eat, drink, and have intercourse after sunset until sleeping or the night prayer, then these acts were forbidden until the next evening; Ibn Abbas's report is graded weak because of Atiyya al-Awfi and those below him.
rows.anchor: أخرجه الطبري 2951 عن ابن عباس بإسناد ضعيف لضعف عطية بن سعد العوفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reported occasion, Umar had intercourse after the night prayer, regretted it, confessed to the Prophet, and other men also admitted doing so before the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال يا رسول الله إني اعتذر إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading makes the wording mean that God permitted intercourse on the night of fasting.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث ) أي أحل الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah's reading الرفوث means explicit speech about what should ordinarily be stated euphemistically.
rows.anchor: وقرا عبد الله ( الرفوث ) وهو الإفصاح بما يجب ان يكنى عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: While in pilgrimage consecration, Ibn Abbas recited a poem with a sexual allusion; when challenged, he said rafath means what occurs with women.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنها انه انشد وهو محرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafath euphemistically denotes intercourse, since intercourse is rarely free of something covered by that term.
rows.anchor: فكنى به عن الجماع لأنه لا يكاد يخلو من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blunt, disapproving term rafath highlights their conduct before permission, which is also called betraying themselves.
rows.anchor: استهجانا لما وجد منهم قبل الإباحة كما سماه اختيانا لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafath is followed by إلى because the verb includes the sense of intimacy and union.
rows.anchor: لتضمينه معنى الإفضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clothing metaphor describes the spouses' close embrace, with each enveloping the other; al-Jaʿdī's poem illustrates it.
rows.anchor: لما كان الرجل والمرأة يعتنقان ويشتمل كل واحد منهما على صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about spouses being garments explains why intercourse was permitted: their intimate closeness makes abstention difficult.
rows.anchor: هو استئناف كالبيان لسبب الاحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Betraying yourselves means wronging yourselves and depriving them of their share of good; the augmented form intensifies the sense of khiyana.
rows.anchor: تظلمونها وتنقصونها حظها من الخير والاختيان من الخيانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turned toward them when they repented from what they had prohibitedly done.
rows.anchor: حين تبتم مما ارتكبتم من المحظور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek the offspring God allotted and recorded through intercourse, rather than seeking pleasure alone, since procreation is a purpose of marriage.
rows.anchor: واطلبوا ما قسم الله لكم وأثبت في اللوح من الولد بالمباشرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the phrase a prohibition of coitus interruptus with free wives.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو نهى عن العزل لأنه في الحرائر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation commands seeking the lawful place of intercourse rather than a forbidden one.
rows.anchor: وقيل وابتغوا المحل الذي كتبه الله لكم وحلله دون ما لم يكتب لكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the words as seeking the permission God granted after the earlier prohibition.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم من الإباحة بعد الحظر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas read واتبعوا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( واتبعوا )

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash read وأتوا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ( وأتوا )

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An interpretation as seeking Laylat al-Qadr and its reward is dismissed by the author as a nearly baseless novelty in exegesis.
rows.anchor: وهو قريب من بدع التفاسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white thread is the first dawn light stretched across the horizon; the black thread is the twilight of night alongside it.
rows.anchor: هو اول من يبدو من الفجر المعترض في الأفق كالخيط الممدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Dawud's line about dawn's thread supplies poetic evidence for this image.
rows.anchor: ولاح من الصبح خيط أنارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From dawn explains the white thread and suffices to clarify the black one; من can also mean that it is part of, and the beginning of, dawn.
rows.anchor: بيان للخيط الأبيض واكتفى به عن بيان الخيط الأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding من dawn turns the expression from metaphor into a vivid simile, just as specifying the source of a lion comparison makes it a simile.
rows.anchor: أخرجه من باب الاستعارة كما ان قولك رأيت أسدا مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added phrase signals the otherwise unclear metaphor and makes the comparison unmistakable, yielding an emphatic simile.
rows.anchor: من شرط المستعار ان يدل عليه الحال أو الكلام ولو لم يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without من الفجر, readers would not know that the two threads are figurative; adding it makes the wording an emphatic simile rather than metaphor.
rows.anchor: فكان تشبيها بليغا وخرج من ان يكون استعارة

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: Adi reports that he put two cords under his pillow and could not distinguish them at night; the Prophet laughed and said his pillow must be broad, or that his nape was broad, meaning daybreak and night.
rows.anchor: عمدت إلى عقالين أبيض وأسود فجعلتهما تحت وسادتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Adi missed the textual clarification and treats the Prophet's reference to his broad nape as a sign of dullness.
rows.anchor: غفل عن البيان ولذلك عرض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous Bedouin poem uses a broad nape as an image of foolishness.
rows.anchor: عريض القفا ميزانه في شماله

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد الساعدي
rows.claim: A report says people tied white and black threads to their legs and ate until they could distinguish them; the phrase من الفجر then clarified that the threads meant day and night.
rows.anchor: فكان رجال إذا أرادوا الصوم ربط احدهم في رجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most jurists and theologians, including Abu Ali and Abu Hashim, reject this report because they disallow delaying clarification of a command.
rows.anchor: وهم اكثر الفقهاء والمتكلمين وهو مذهب أبي علي وأبي هاشم فلم يصح عندهم هذا الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who allow delayed clarification say the initial wording still informs the listener of an obligation and prompts readiness to act once its meaning is clarified.
rows.anchor: ليس بعبث لأن المخاطب يستفيد منه وجوب الخطاب ويعزم على فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to complete the fast until night supports daytime intention for Ramadan, delaying the purificatory bath until dawn, and rejecting continuous fasting.
rows.anchor: فيه دليل على جواز النية بالنهار في صوم رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtikaf means keeping oneself in a mosque for worship.
rows.anchor: والاعتكاف ان يحبس نفسه في المسجد يتعبد فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here direct contact means intercourse, as in the earlier permission; a further view includes lustful touching, and intercourse or touching or kissing followed by emission invalidates iʿtikaf.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالمباشرة الجماع لما تقدم من قوله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says a man in iʿtikaf used to leave, have intercourse with his wife, and return to the mosque, which God then forbade.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة كان الرجل اذا اعتكف خرج فباشر امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage indicates iʿtikaf must take place in a mosque, without limiting it to a particular mosque; other views restrict it to a prophet's mosque or a congregational mosque, while the majority require a mosque where congregational prayer is held.
rows.anchor: وقالوا فيه دليل على ان الإعتكاف لا يكون الا في مسجد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid read في المسجد in the singular.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ( في المسجد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those boundaries refer to the rulings just mentioned.
rows.anchor: الأحكام التي ذكرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are within the sphere of truth; they are told not to cross its boundary, then more emphatically not even to approach it, so they stay far from falsehood.
rows.anchor: فنهى ان يتعداه لأن من تعداه وقع في حيز الباطل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compares God's prohibitions to a king's protected pasture: someone grazing around it may soon enter it; the author equates grazing nearby with approaching the boundary.
rows.anchor: إن لكل ملك حمى وحمى الله محارمه فمن رتع حول الحمى يوشك أن يقع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's boundaries can specifically mean prohibitions and bans, as illustrated by the restriction on marital intercourse during iʿtikaf.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يريد بحدود الله محارمه ومناهيه خصوصا لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question expresses amazement at Nimrod's disputation about God and his disbelief.
rows.anchor: تعجيب من محاجة نمروذ في الله وكفره به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grant of kingship may explain his dispute because it made him arrogant and tyrannical, or because he perversely disputed instead of thanking God for the gift.
rows.anchor: ايتاء الملك أبطره واورثه الكبر والعتو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means that Nimrod disputed at the time God gave him kingship.
rows.anchor: والاني حاج وقت أن آتاه الله الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's granting kingship to an unbeliever may mean granting the wealth, servants, and followers by which he became dominant, without divine empowerment to prevail.
rows.anchor: آتاه ما غلب به وتسلط من المال والخدم والأتباع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God made him king as a test for His servants.
rows.anchor: وقيل ملكه امتحانا لعباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause إذ قال is governed by حاج, or it substitutes for the time clause in آتاه because آتاه is construed as a time expression.
rows.anchor: نصب بحاج أو بدل من آتاه اذ جعل بمعنى الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod's claim to give life and death means that he pardons one condemned to die and kills another.
rows.anchor: يريد أعفو عن القتل وأقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim changed to a proof Nimrod could not answer after hearing his foolish reply, demonstrating that a debater may move from one argument to another.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على جواز الانتقال للمجادل من حجة إلى حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading of فبهت is explained as Ibrahim having defeated the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( فبهت الذي كفر ) أي فغلب إبراهيم الكافر

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa read فبهت on the pattern of qaruba; another explanation takes it to mean that the unbeliever was confounded.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة ( فبهت ) بوزن قرب وقيل كانت هذه المحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account dates the dispute to after Abraham broke the idols and Nimrod imprisoned him, then released him to be burned and asked who his Lord was.
rows.anchor: كانت هذه المحاجة حين كسر الأصنام وسجنه نمروذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase أو كالذي means ‘or did you see one like him’; أرأيت is omitted because ألم تر already signals the exclamatory construction.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يحمل على المعنى دون اللفظ كانه قيل أرأيت كالذي حاج إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By sense, it may mean ‘or like the one who disputed Abraham,’ or ‘or like the passerby’; the latter was apparently an unbeliever, in parallel with Nimrod and the expression of incredulity.
rows.anchor: والمار كان كافرا بالبعث وهو الظاهر لانتظامه مع نمروذ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the passerby as Ezra or al-Khidr, who wanted to witness resurrection and increase his certainty, like Abraham.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو عزير أو الخضر أراد ان يعاين احياء الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passerby's question ‘how?’ acknowledges that he cannot know the manner of revival and magnifies the reviver's power.
rows.anchor: اعتراف بالعجز عن معرفة طريقة الاحياء واستعظام لقدرة المحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruined village is Jerusalem when Nebuchadnezzar destroyed it; another view identifies it as the village from which thousands departed.
rows.anchor: والقرية بيت المقدس حين خربه بختنصر وقيل هي التي خرج منها الألوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He estimated that a day or part of one had passed because he died in the morning and was raised a century later before sunset; seeing the remaining sun corrected his estimate.
rows.anchor: روي انه مات ضحى وبعث بعد مائة سنة قبل غيبوبة الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says his food was figs and grapes and his drink juice or milk; the fruit seemed freshly picked and the drink unchanged.
rows.anchor: وروي أن طعامه كان تينا وعنبا وشرابه عصيرا أو لبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم يتسنه means the food did not change; its final ه may be a root letter or pause suffix, with an etymology from year because things change over time.
rows.anchor: لم يتغير والهاء أصلية أو هاء سكت واشتقاقه من السنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative derives the word from putrid mud, with one n assimilated into a weak letter.
rows.anchor: وقيل أصله يتسنن من الحمأ المسنون فقلبت نونه حرف علة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food had not aged through the century and remained as it was, as though a hundred years had not passed.
rows.anchor: لم تمر عليه السنون التى مرت عليه يعني هو بحاله كما كان

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah's reading has ‘this is your drink’ and omits the final h in لم يتسن.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله ( فانظر إلى طعامك وهذا شرابك لم يتسن )

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy read لم يسنه, assimilating the tāʾ into the sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( لم يسنه ) بإدغام التاء في السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey's bones had scattered and decayed; alternatively, it remained alive where tied for a century without food or water, like the preserved food and drink.
rows.anchor: كيف تفرقت عظامه ونخرت وكان له حمار قد ربطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Ezra returned on his donkey and recited the Torah from memory while the people checked it, prompting them to call him God's son; another says his children had aged while he remained young.
rows.anchor: وقيل أتى قومه راكب حماره وقال انا عزير فكذبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bones may be the donkey's bones or those of the dead whose revival had amazed the passerby.
rows.anchor: هي عظام الحمار أو عظام الموتى الذين تعجب من إحيائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ننشزها means reassembling by moving and raising bones into place; al-Hasan's ننشرها derives from God's raising the dead.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( ننشرها ) من نشر الله الموتى بمعنى أنشرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of تبين is omitted and understood as ‘that God is powerful over all things,’ indicated by the following statement; alternatively, what became clear was resurrection itself.
rows.anchor: مضمر تقديره فلما تبين له ان الله على كل شيء قدير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas read فلما تبين له in the passive voice; another reading has an imperative ‘know,’ while Abdullah's reading has ‘it was said: know.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ( فلما تبين له ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the passerby had been an unbeliever, God could address him after raising him, when he was no longer an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: كان الكلام بعد البعث ولم يكن اذ ذاك كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable omits a genitive: either the givers' expenditure is like a seed, or the givers are like someone sowing a seed; God truly causes growth, though it is attributed to seed, earth, or water as causes.
rows.anchor: لا بد من حذف مضاف أي مثل نفقتهم كمثل حبة أو مثلهم كمثل باذر حبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grain grows a stalk with seven branches and an ear on each; the image makes multiplied reward visible to the observer.
rows.anchor: تخرج ساقا يتشعب منها سبع شعب لكل واحدة سنبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image is found in millet and sorghum, and wheat stalks can sometimes branch to that yield in fertile fields; even if unattested, a hypothetical image is valid.
rows.anchor: بل هو موجود في الدخن والذرة وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural سنابل rather than the expected paucity form سنبلات is acceptable because plural patterns can substitute for one another, as discussed for qurūʾ.
rows.anchor: من وقوع أمثله الجمع متعاورة مواقعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God multiplies the reward for whoever He wills, not every giver, because givers' circumstances differ; alternatively, He may increase the seven hundredfold further for those who merit it.
rows.anchor: لا لكل منفق لتفاوت احوال المنفقين أو يضاعف سبع المائة ويزيد عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is to remind the recipient of his favor and claim that he created an obligation; Arab advice says to forget good deeds, as a poem warns.
rows.anchor: المن أن يعتد على من احسن اليه بإحسانه ويريد أنه اصطنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm means acting superior to the recipient because of what one gave; a proverb contrasts the sweetness of generosity with the bitterness of reminding someone.
rows.anchor: والأذى ان يتطاول عليه بسبب ما ازال اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks the gap between giving and refraining from reminders: refraining is better than the act of giving itself, just as steadfastness is better than entering faith.
rows.anchor: إظهار التفاوت بين الانفاق وترك المن والأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause lacks fa because its relative does not imply a condition; in the later clause, fa signals that giving earns the reward, a link absent without it.
rows.anchor: الموصول لم يضمن ههنا معنى الشرط وضمنه ثمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A good word means a courteous, gracious reply.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قول معروف ﴾ رد جميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness may mean excusing an irritating petitioner, God's forgiveness earned by a gentle refusal, or the petitioner's forgiving the refusal.
rows.anchor: وعفو عن السائل اذا وجد منه ما يثقل على المسؤل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite subject can be predicated of as ‘better’ because its descriptive qualification makes it specific.
rows.anchor: وصح الاخبار عن المبتدأ النكرة لاختصاصه بالصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no need of a giver who reminds and harms, and His forbearance delays immediate punishment; this restraint signals displeasure and threat.
rows.anchor: لا حاجة به إلى منفق يمن ويؤذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning compares nullifying charity by reminders and harm to a hypocrite's giving for public display without seeking God's pleasure or afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: أي لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى كإبطال المنافق

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib read صفوان on the pattern of كروان.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن المسيب ( صفوان ) بوزن كروان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wabil is rain with large drops.
rows.anchor: مطر عظيم القطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣald means stripped bare of its soil, as in describing the shining bald forehead.
rows.anchor: أجرد نقيا من التراب الذي كان عليه ومنه صلد جبين الأصلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their earned deeds yield nothing, like dust scattered away.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فجعلناه هباء منثورا ﴾ الفرقان 23

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison can be circumstantial: do not invalidate charity while resembling the person who spends in ostentation.
rows.anchor: ان تكون الكاف في محل النصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ‘they cannot’ refers to the class or group of spenders; al-ladhī and man alternate in meaning.
rows.anchor: أراد بالذي ينفق الجنس أو الفريق الذي ينفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving wealth, a close companion to life and especially difficult to surrender, disciplines the self, humbles it, restrains desire, and steadies faith and certainty.
rows.anchor: وليثبتوا منها ببذل المال الذي هو شقيق الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means confirming Islam and the reward from sincere hearts, since spending for God shows genuine belief in recompense.
rows.anchor: وتصديقا للإسلام وتحقيقا للجزاء من أصل انفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, من is partitive, as in ‘he stirred some of his energy’; on the second it marks a starting point, as in envy from within themselves.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثاني لابتداء الغاية كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid's reading وتبيينا من أنفسهم supports the interpretation that their spending demonstrates sincere faith to other believers.
rows.anchor: وتعضده قراءة مجاهد ( وتبيينا من أنفسهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving wealth establishes a part of oneself, while giving both wealth and life establishes the whole self.
rows.anchor: ومن بذل ماله وروحه معا فهو الذي ثبتها كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage connects steadfastness to striving for God's cause with wealth and selves.
rows.anchor: وتجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالكم وأنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The givers' expenditure grows in God's regard like a garden on high ground, where trees produce better and finer fruit.
rows.anchor: بمكان مرتفع وخصها لأن الشجر فيها ازكى وأحسن ثمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wabil means heavy rain, akul means its crop, double means twice the yield, and a light drizzle suffices because the garden's soil is fertile.
rows.anchor: مثلي ما كانت تثمر بسبب الوابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the people are like the garden, and abundant or modest expenditure is like heavy rain or drizzle; either yields multiplied fruit when spent sincerely and fully.
rows.anchor: أو مثل حالهم عند الله بالجنة على الربوة ونفقتهم الكثيرة والقليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include كمثل حبة, the word rabwa with three vowel patterns, and أكلها with two dammas.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( كمثل حبة ) وبربوة ) بالحركات الثلاث وأكلها ) بضمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza expresses disapproval; readings also have ‘gardens’ and ‘weak offspring.’
rows.anchor: للإنكار وقرىء له جنات وذرية ضعاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An iʿṣār is a rotating wind that rises from the ground like a column into the sky.
rows.anchor: الريح التى تستدير في الأرض ثم تسطع نحو السماء كالعمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image concerns good deeds done without seeking God: on Judgment Day they are found void, producing the devastation of an elderly person whose dependent children lose their livelihood.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل لمن يعمل الأعمال الحسنة لا يبتغي بها وجه الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked by Umar, Ibn Abbas interprets the image as a wealthy person whose good deeds are later drowned by sins after Satan leads him astray.
rows.anchor: قال ضربت مثلا لعمل قال لأي عمل قال لرجل غني يعمل الحسنات

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the old person with many children is most in need of his garden, just as a believer is most in need of his deeds when worldly life ends.
rows.anchor: وإن احدكم والله أفقر ما يكون إلى عمله اذا انقطعت عنه الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Palms and vines are singled out as the noblest and most useful trees, though the garden contains others; all fruits are then added.
rows.anchor: لما كانا اكرم الشجر وأكثرها منافع خصهما بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruits may mean all the benefits of the garden, as in the story of the two gardens in al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يريد بالثمرات المنافع التي كانت تحصل له فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction before ‘old age struck him’ can be circumstantial; alternatively, the wording follows the meaning of ‘would one wish if he had a garden and had grown old?’
rows.anchor: قلت الواو للحال لا للعطف ومعناه ان تكون له جنة وقد أصابه الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good things earned means the finest of one's earnings.
rows.anchor: من جياد مكسوباتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God brings from the earth includes grain, fruit, minerals, and other products.
rows.anchor: من الحب والثمر والمعادن وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘good things’ is omitted before what comes from the earth because the preceding mention already supplies it.
rows.anchor: الا انه حذف لذكر الطيبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not deliberately select inferior wealth to spend, specifying it as the item for charity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تيمموا الخبيث ﴾ ولا تقصدوا المال الرديء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abdullah and Ibn Abbas have variant readings of ولا تيمموا; the forms yimma, tayammama, and taʾammama all mean to intend.
rows.anchor: ويممه وتيممه وتاممه سواء في معنى قصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You would not accept such inferior wealth in settling your own rights.
rows.anchor: وحالكم أنكم لا تأخذونه في حقوقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Overlooking it means tolerating it as payment; the metaphor comes from lowering one's gaze, and merchants say not to insist on full value.
rows.anchor: الا بأن تتسامحوا في أخذه وتترخصوا فيه

rows.speaker: الطرماح
rows.claim: Al-Tirimmāḥ's verse attests to accepting injury or deficiency by overlooking it.
rows.anchor: وللضيم رجال يرضون بالاغماض

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri read تغمضوا; variants أغمض and غمض have the same meaning, and another vocalization is reported.
rows.anchor: وقرا الزهري ( تغمضوا ) وأغمض وغمض بمعنى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada's passive reading means being compelled to accept or to be found accepting it with one's eyes shut.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة ( تغمضوا ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says one would not buy such goods at market unless their price were reduced.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن رضي الله عنه لو وجدتموه في السوق يباع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they used to give the worst dates, and were forbidden to do so.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كانوا يتصدقون بحشف التمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the context of spending, Satan predicts that giving will leave people poor.
rows.anchor: أي يعدكم في الانفاق ﴿ الفقر ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word poverty has readings with a damma or two fathas.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( الفقر ) بالضم ( والفقر ) بفتحتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A promise can concern either good or evil, as the Qur'an also says of Hell.
rows.anchor: والوعد يستعمل في الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan commands miserliness and withholding charity; Arabs call a miser fāḥish.
rows.anchor: ويغريكم على البخل ومنع الصدقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises forgiveness and expiation, plus replacement better than the gift or a reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ﴿ مغفرة ﴾ لذنوبكم وكفارة لها ﴿ وفضلا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirr is a cold wind, supported by poetry using ṣirr and ṣarṣar.
rows.anchor: الصر الريح الباردة نحو الصرصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may describe the wind as cold in an emphatic way, use ṣirr as a verbal noun for cold, or follow an idiom in which something is ‘in’ another, as in the cited line about God sustaining the weak.
rows.anchor: أن الصر في صفة الريح بمعنى الباردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spenders' wealth served status, public praise, and remembrance rather than God's approval, like a crop ruined by cold.
rows.anchor: شبه ما كانوا ينفقون من اموالهم في المكارم والمفاخر وكسب الثناء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the comparison concerns what they spent to seek nearness to God despite their disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو ما كانوا يتقربون به إلى الله مع كفرهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says their spending against the Prophet was wasted because it did not achieve their intended purpose.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما أنفقوا في عداوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فضاع عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop owners' injustice makes its destruction a punishment, more severe than an ordinary loss because it comes from divine anger.
rows.anchor: فأهلك عقوبة لهم على معاصيهم لأن الهلاك عن سخط أشد وأبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is a compound simile, as in the parable of the fire-lighter; alternatively, it compares the destruction of spending to a wind's destruction or the spending to a destructive wind.
rows.anchor: من التشبيه المركب الذي مر في تفسير قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading addresses the audience directly with تنفقون.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( تنفقون بالتاء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘God did not wrong them’ may refer to the spenders, who made their gifts undeserving of acceptance, or to crop owners who deserved punishment.
rows.anchor: الضمير للمنفقين على معنى وما ظلمهم الله بان لم يقبل نفقاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled reading ولكن means ‘rather, they wrong themselves’; omitting its object pronoun is allowed only in poetry.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ولكن ) بالتشديد بمعنى ولكن انفسهم يظلمونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ reading supplies an omitted noun, ‘the miserliness of those who are miserly’; with yāʾ, the subject may be the Messenger or another person, or the misers themselves with an omitted first object.
rows.anchor: من قرأ بالتاء قدر مضافا محذوفا أي ولا تحسبن بخل الذين يبخلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object is licensed by the nearby verb يبخلون; هو is a separator pronoun, and al-Aʿmash omitted it.
rows.anchor: عليه وهو فصل وقرأ الأعمش بغير هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being ‘collared’ explains the evil of miserliness as bearing its consequence like a collar; an Arabic proverb uses the image for disgrace.
rows.anchor: أي سيلزمون وبال ما بخلوا به الزام الطوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says withheld zakat becomes a snake around the miser's neck, biting and speaking; the Prophet describes a hairless snake, with another report specifying a black one.
rows.anchor: وقيل يجعل ما بخل من الزكاة حية يطوقها في عنقه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the one who withholds zakat will be collared by a hairless serpent; another transmitted wording says a black serpent.
rows.anchor: 230 ( يطوق بشجاع أقرع )

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi interprets the collar as a collar of fire.
rows.anchor: وعن النخعي سيطوقون بطوق من نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns what the heavens and earth contain and what their inhabitants inherit; hoarding His property rather than spending it in His cause is irrational.
rows.anchor: فمالهم يبخلون عليه بملكه ولا ينفقونه في سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument parallels the command to spend from what God made people stewards over.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قوله ﴿ وأنفقوا مما جعلكم مستخلفين فيه ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ reading shifts to direct address and heightens the threat; the yāʾ reading follows the preceding third-person form.
rows.anchor: فالتاء على طريقة الالتفات وهي أبلغ في الوعيد والياء على الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns the heavens and earth, controls people's affairs, and has power to punish them.
rows.anchor: فهو يملك امرهم وهو على كل شيء قدير فهو يقدر على عقابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmic signs clearly evidence the Creator, His immense power, and His striking wisdom.
rows.anchor: لأدلة واضحة على الصانع وعظيم قدرته وباهر حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of understanding look with insight, reasoning, and reflection rather than gazing like heedless animals.
rows.anchor: للذين يفتحون بصائرهم للنظر والاستدلال والاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A short admonition urges people to study the stars and wonders of the universe, reflecting on their maker's power and wisdom before death ends the chance.
rows.anchor: املأ عينيك من زينة هذه الكواكب وأجلهما في جملة هذه العجائب

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports asking Aisha about what most amazed her in the Prophet; she begins an account of his night worship, prayer, and weeping, continued in the next segment.
rows.anchor: قلت لعائشة رضي الله عنها أخبريني بأعجب ما رأيت

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha recounts that the Prophet sought her permission for night worship, prayed and wept, and told Bilal he wept because God had sent down the signs of creation; he warned against reciting without reflection.
rows.anchor: ثم قال ويل لمن قرأها ولم يتفكر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report warns against mouthing the verse between one's jaws without contemplating it; no named authority or grading is given.
rows.anchor: 237 ( ويل لمن لاكها بين فكيه ولم يتاملها )

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that when the Prophet rose at night, he used a toothstick, looked toward the sky, and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قام من الليل يتسوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says an Israelite's cloud of shade failed after thirty years of worship; his mother attributes it to once looking at the sky without reflecting.
rows.anchor: قالت لعلك نظرت مرة إلى السماء ولم تعتبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who remember God do so continually while standing, sitting, or lying down, and rarely leave remembrance in their lives.
rows.anchor: ذكرا دائبا على أي حال كانوا من قيام وقعود واضطجاع

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وعروة بن الزبير وجماعة
rows.claim: Ibn Umar, Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, and others went to the Eid prayer ground remembering God, then one of them began to cite this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر وعروة بن الزبير وجماعة انهم خرجوا يوم العيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning those Muslims who are not yet devout, the text turns to the devout: draw them near and honor them, and do not obey those seeking the opposite.
rows.anchor: ثم أردفهم ذكر المتقين منهم وأمره بتقريبهم وإكرامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on their Lord morning and evening means continuous worship; alternatively it specifically means the dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه : يصلون صلاة الصبح والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's face denotes sincerity; ‘face’ can express a thing's essence and reality.
rows.anchor: ووسمهم بالإخلاص في عبادتهم بقوله

rows.speaker: رؤسا من المشركين
rows.claim: Polytheist leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor believers such as Ammar, Suhayb, Bilal, Khabbab, and Salman so they could speak with him; he refused, then briefly considered their request in hope they might believe, before revelation forbade it.
rows.anchor: لو طردت عنا هؤلاء الأعبد يعنون فقراء المسلمين

rows.speaker: سلمان وخباب
rows.claim: Salman and Khabbab say this was revealed about them: the Prophet sat very close, then revelation told him to remain with them until they rose; he praised God for living to receive that command.
rows.anchor: قال سلمان وخباب : فينا نزلت فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accounting clauses assure the Prophet that allegations about the believers do not bind him: he judges outward signs, and any hidden fault remains their burden, as in the rule that no bearer bears another's burden.
rows.anchor: فما يلزمك إلا اعتبار الظاهر والاتسام بسيمة المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both accounting clauses are needed together to convey that neither group is answerable for the other's account.
rows.anchor: ولا يستقل بهذا المعنى إلا الجملتان جميعا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the pronouns to refer to the polytheists: they are not responsible for the Prophet's account nor he for theirs, so eagerness for their conversion must not lead him to expel believers.
rows.anchor: لا يؤاخذون بحسابك ولا أنت بحسابهم ، حتى يهمك إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the syntax, فتطردهم responds to the negation and فتكون to the prohibition; alternatively, it coordinates as a consequence because injustice results from expelling them.
rows.anchor: جواب النهي . ويجوز أن يكون عطفا على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has بالغدوة والعشي.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( بالغدوة والعشي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive verb ‘were sent’ is grammatically attached to the prepositional phrase ‘to them’; the nations are questioned about their response to messengers, and messengers about the response they received.
rows.anchor: مسند إلى الجار والمجرور وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recounts their deeds and words with full knowledge and was absent from none of their affairs.
rows.anchor: عالمين بأحوالهم الظاهرة والباطنة وأقوالهم وأفعالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioning is for rebuke, reprimand, and confirmation when people state their answers and the prophets testify.
rows.anchor: معناه التوبيخ والتقريع والتقرير إذا فاهوا به ألسنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawāḥish are acts whose ugliness has grown extreme, or specifically sexual sins; ithm is any sin, or specifically wine; baghy is injustice and arrogance.
rows.anchor: ما تفاحش قبحه أي تزايد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God not sending authority for association is ironic, since no proof can authorize worshipping another with Him.
rows.anchor: فيه تهكم ، لأنه لا يجوز أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking falsely about God means fabricating claims about what He has prohibited and similar matters.
rows.anchor: وأن تتقولوا عليه وتفتروا الكذب من التحريم وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukāʾ is a verbal noun-pattern word from whistling and names their frequent whistling; a shortened reading parallels the forms for weeping.
rows.anchor: المكاء : فعال بوزن الثغاء والرغاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣdiya means clapping, derived either from ṣadā or the verb ṣadda, as in the cited Qur'anic phrase.
rows.anchor: والتصدية : التصفيق ، تفعلة من الصدى أو من صد يصد

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash read صلاتهم in the accusative, with the predicate of kāna preceding its subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش : ( وما كان صلاتهم ) بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording exchanges expected roles: they put whistling and clapping in place of prayer, as the cited poem puts chains and spears in place of gifts.
rows.anchor: ووضعوا المكاء والتصدية موضع الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They circled the House naked, whistling through interlocked fingers and clapping; they also disrupted the Prophet's prayer and recitation this way.
rows.anchor: يطوفون بالبيت عراة : الرجال والنساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to taste punishment refers to the killing and capture at Badr as consequences of their disbelief and deeds.
rows.anchor: عذاب القتل والأسر يوم بدر ، بسبب كفركم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One occasion report says each of the men who provisioned the Badr army supplied ten camels daily.
rows.anchor: نزلت في المطعمين يوم بدر ، كان يطعم كل واحد منهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says traders in the caravan were asked to fund a war on Muhammad to avenge losses at Badr.
rows.anchor: قالوا لكل من كان له تجارة في العير : أعينوا بهذا المال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third says the verse concerns Abu Sufyan, who hired two thousand allies for Uhud and paid them forty ūqiyyas, each worth forty-two mithqals.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي سفيان وقد استأجر ليوم أحد ألفين من الأحابيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their intended purpose was to block people from following Muhammad, God's path, even if they themselves did not understand it that way.
rows.anchor: أي كان غرضهم في الإنفاق الصد عن اتباع محمد وهو سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their spending's outcome becomes regret, as though the spending itself turns into regret and grief.
rows.anchor: أي تكون عاقبة إنفاقها ندما وحسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are ultimately defeated, even if the war's fortunes had previously alternated, and some later became Muslims.
rows.anchor: آخر الأمر وإن كانت الحرب بينهم وبين المؤمنين سجالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers among them are gathered to Hell, since some others accepted Islam well.
rows.anchor: لأن منهم من أسلم وحسن إسلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse distinguishes the unbelieving group from the believers and heaps the vile together until they are piled up, as in the image of piled crowds.
rows.anchor: الفريق الخبيث من الكفار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it separates the ill-gotten money spent against the Prophet from the good money spent by Abu Bakr and Uthman to support him, then consigns the former to Hell with its owners.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ليميز المال الخبيث الذي أنفقه المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the main reading, the lām attaches to ‘they will be gathered’; under the alternative, it attaches to ‘it becomes regret.’ The reading ليميز is lightened.
rows.anchor: واللام على هذا متعلقة بقوله : { ثم تكون عليهم حسرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three are Kaʿb ibn Malik, Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ, and Hilal ibn Umayya.
rows.anchor: كعب بن مالك ، ومرارة بن الربيع ، وهلال بن أمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were left behind from the expedition; alternatively, they lagged behind Abu Lubaba and his companions, whose repentance had been accepted earlier.
rows.anchor: خلفوا عن الغزو وقيل عن أبي لبابة وأصحابه حين تيب عليهم بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include ‘they were left behind’ or ‘they left the warriors in Medina’; Jaʿfar al-Sadiq read خالفوا, and al-Aʿmash read المخلفين.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( خلفوا ) أي خلفوا الغازين بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth being spacious yet constricted is a metaphor for their bewilderment and agitation, unable to settle anywhere.
rows.anchor: وهو مثل للحيرة في أمرهم ، كأنهم لا يجدون فيها مكانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their selves means their hearts, which could hold no comfort or joy because of their loneliness and grief.
rows.anchor: أي قلوبهم ، لا يسعها أنس ولا سرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They thought’ means they knew there was no refuge from God's anger except turning to Him for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وعلموا { أن لا ملجأ من } سخط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeatedly accepted them with mercy so they would persist in repentance and repent again after future slips, since He accepts repeated repentance.
rows.anchor: ثم رجع عليهم بالقبول والرحمة كرة بعد أخرى ، ليستقيموا على توبتهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan recounts three believers who gave up a valuable orchard, attachment to family, or love of life and joined the Prophet; he concludes believers repent without persisting in sin.
rows.anchor: بلغني أنه كان لأحدهم حائط كان خيرا من مائة ألف درهم

rows.speaker: أبو ذر الغفاري
rows.claim: Abu Dharr's camel lagged, so he carried his belongings and followed the Prophet on foot; the Prophet prayed that Abu Dharr walk, die, and be raised alone, with mercy.
rows.anchor: أن بعيره أبطأ به فحمل متاعه على ظهره

rows.speaker: أبو خيثمة
rows.claim: Abu Khaythama left his shaded garden, fresh dates, cold water, and beautiful wife to catch the Prophet; the Prophet recognized the approaching rider and rejoiced.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي خيثمة أنه بلغ بستانه وكانت له امرأة حسناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three remained behind and did not catch up with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من بقي لم يلحق به . منهم الثلاثة

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb recounts the Prophet's stern response on his return, the community's silence, separation from wives after forty nights, and the announcement after fifty nights that God had accepted them; he prostrated, was greeted by Talha, and heard the Prophet call it his best day since birth.
rows.anchor: قال كعب : لما قفل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سلمت عليه فرد علي كالمغضب

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq defines sincere repentance as feeling the earth and one's own soul constrict, like Kaʿb and his two companions.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بكر الوراق أنه سئل عن التوبة النصوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not deprive people of anything serving their interests, including messengers and revealed books; they wrong themselves through disbelief and denial.
rows.anchor: لا ينقصهم شيئا مما يتصل بمصالحهم من بعثة الرسل وإنزال الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the statement warns the deniers that their justly deserved punishment results from their own deeds, not divine injustice.
rows.anchor: أن ما يلحقهم يوم القيامة من العذاب لاحق بهم على سبيل العدل

none: verse text only; the segment contains no commentary

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each nation receives a messenger to call it to God's oneness and true religion; when denied after clear proofs, God judges fairly, saving the messenger and punishing the rejecters.
rows.anchor: يبعث إليهم لينبههم على التوحيد ، ويدعوهم إلى دين الحق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, each nation has a messenger identified with it at Judgment Day, testifying to its belief or disbelief.
rows.anchor: أو لكل أمة من الأمم يوم القيامة رسول تنسب إليه وتدعى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers ask impatiently when the promised punishment will arrive, treating it as unlikely.
rows.anchor: استعجال لما وعدوا من العذاب استبعادا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot independently bring himself harm such as illness or poverty, or benefit such as health or wealth; the exception is disconnected, meaning whatever God wills happens.
rows.anchor: من صحة أو غنى { إلا ما شاء الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each nation has a fixed term for punishment, fulfilled without fail, so they should not demand it early.
rows.anchor: يعني أن عذابكم له أجل مضروب عند الله وحد محدود من الزمان

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin read فإذا جاء آجالهم with the plural ‘terms.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن سيرين : ( فإذا جاء آجالهم )

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan read وجوزنا, from a verb meaning to cross or traverse a place; this differs from the verb in al-Aʿsha's line, which would instead take بني إسرائيل as its object.
rows.anchor: وجوزنا من أجاز المكان وجوزه وجاوزه

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: The poet al-Aʿsha's line وإذا تجوزنا حبال قبيلة illustrates a different verb from the reading وجوزنا.
rows.anchor: بيت الأعشى : وإذا تجوزنا حبال قبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading has the syntax of making the Israelites cross the sea, as in the cited poetic comparison of crossing a spear through a door.
rows.anchor: لو كان منه لكان حقه أن يقال وجوزنا بني إسرائيل في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh repeated one meaning in three formulations in hope of acceptance, but his confession was rejected because he spoke after choice and moral responsibility had ended.
rows.anchor: كرر المخذول المعنى الواحد ثلاث مرات في ثلاث عبارات حرصا على القبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Now?’ questions faith at the moment of desperation, when drowning has overtaken him and he has lost hope; views differ whether he spoke as he choked, just before drowning, or after internally drowning.
rows.anchor: أتؤمن الساعة في وقت الاضطرار حين أدركك الغرق وأيست من نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story that Gabriel stuffed sea mud into Pharaoh's mouth is a blasphemous fabrication, not an obstacle to heartfelt faith; hating an unbeliever's faith itself amounts to disbelief.
rows.anchor: فمن زيادات الباهتين لله وملائكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two objections to the mud story are that faith is valid in the heart even for a mute person, and that one who prefers an unbeliever to remain disbelieving is himself an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: أن الإيمان يصح بالقلب كإيمان الأخرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mufsidin means those who are astray and lead others away from faith.
rows.anchor: من الضالين المضلين عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel asked Pharaoh for a ruling about a servant raised in his master's wealth who denied his benefactor and claimed mastery; Pharaoh wrote that such a rebel should drown, and Gabriel showed him the ruling as he drowned.
rows.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام أتاه بفتيا : ما قول الأمير في عبد لرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ‘We shall save you’ has doubled and light readings; it can mean removing Pharaoh from the deep where his people drowned or casting him onto high ground.
rows.anchor: بالتشديد والتخفيف : نبعدك مما وقع فيه قومك من قعر البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading with ḥāʾ means casting him to the sea's edge; Kaʿb says the water threw his body ashore like a bull.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ننحيك ) بالحاء : نلقيك بناحية مما يلي البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘With your body’ may mean a lifeless body, a complete unchanged body, naked, or wearing his armor.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال ، أي : في الحال التي لا روح فيك

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معديكرب
rows.claim: Amr ibn Maʿdikarib's poem illustrates the bodily or armor reading of ببدنك.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن معديكرب : أعاذل شكتي بدني وسيفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is in the heavens and earth means their signs and lessons; signs and warners cannot benefit people who are not expected to believe.
rows.anchor: من الآيات والعبر { وما تغنى الآيات والنذر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning refers either to messengers who warn or to warnings themselves; the people addressed do not reason or believe.
rows.anchor: والرسل المنذرون . أو الإنذارات { عن قوم لا يؤمنون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has يغني with yāʾ; ما is then either negative or interrogative.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : وما يغني بالياء ، و ( ما ) نافية ، أو استفهامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘days’ of former peoples are God's episodes of punishment, as ‘the Days of the Arabs’ means their battles.
rows.anchor: وقائع الله تعالى فيهم . كما يقال : ( أيام العرب ) لوقائعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Then We save’ coordinates with an omitted statement: God destroys nations, then saves messengers, recounting past events.
rows.anchor: معطوف على كلام محذوف يدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers saved are those who believed with the messengers; similarly God will rescue believers and destroy polytheists.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الإنجاء ننجي المؤمنين منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘An obligation upon Us’ is parenthetical emphasis that this rescue is truly binding upon God.
rows.anchor: اعتراض ، يعني : حق ذلك علينا حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has ننج with a doubled jīm.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ننج ) بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who seek worldly life receive the full wages of their deeds in this world, including health and provision, without any reduction.
rows.anchor: نوصل إليهم أجور أعمالهم وافية كاملة من غير بخس في الدنيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies them as ostentatious people: reciters, charitable kin-keepers, and fighters each sought a reputation and got it.
rows.anchor: هم أهل الرياء . يقال للقراء منهم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas says they are Jews and Christians: charitable giving and kinship earned them immediate reward through greater provision and bodily health.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك : هم اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they are hypocrites who joined the Prophet's campaigns and received a share of the spoils.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هم الذين جاهدوا من المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include يوف with yāʾ, making God the subject; تُوفَ with tāʾ in the passive; and al-Hasan's light نوفي with yāʾ because the conditional verb is past.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يوف ) بالياء على أن الفعل لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘By the name of God’ means that the ship's movement and docking occur by His power and command.
rows.anchor: بالله إجراؤها وإرساؤها ، أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has مجراها and مرساها with an open mīm, analyzed as verbal nouns, times, or places.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { مجراها ومرساها } بفتح الميم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid read مجريها مرسيها as active participles in the genitive, describing God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد { * مجريها ومرسيها } بلفظ اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be an inserted sentence: Noah tells them to board, then says the ship's course and anchoring are by God's name, command, and power.
rows.anchor: معناه أن نوحا عليه السلام أمرهم بالركوب ، ثم أخبرهم بأن مجراها ومرساها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a circumstantial phrase modifying the ship, meaning it was made to sail and anchor by God's name; compare the command to enter Paradise eternally.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون غير مقتضيه بأن تكون في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgiveness and mercy are why He saved Noah's people; without them they would not have been rescued.
rows.anchor: لولا مغفرته لذنوبكم ورحمته إياكم لما نجاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin in كلا substitutes for a genitive, meaning all of them; a suppressed oath governs the promise that God will repay everyone's good and bad deeds, belief and denial.
rows.anchor: التنوين عوض من المضاف إليه ، يعني : وإن كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لما marks the oath and ما is extra; the light reading of إن treats it like its emphatic form.
rows.anchor: موطئة للقسم ، و { ما } مزيدة والمعنى

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading makes إن negative and لما mean ‘except’; Abdullah's reading clarifies it as ‘everyone will surely be repaid.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي : ( وإن كل لما ليوفينهم )

rows.speaker: الزهري وسليمان بن أرقم
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri and Sulayman ibn Arqam read with tanwin, meaning everyone assembled together, like ‘they all prostrated.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وسليمان بن أرقم ( وإن كلا لما ليوفينهم ) بالتنوين
